why: A random direction of matched norm has about 1/700 of the RL delta's KL, so at T 1.0 (no loops to break) the edited model behaves as the cued base resampled, about 410.
With KL near zero the random cell is a resample of the cued base, so it fixes only the base's own resample rate (about a third) of its 90 wrong problems.
A near-zero-KL random edit leaves generation length at the cued base's 3,933 tokens per problem.

The RL delta is small and in the quadratic regime, so a = 1.5 adds only about a quarter of RL's KL beyond RL (about 0.2 nats per token from base, far below the ~1 nat per token cliff), keeping accuracy near RL's level.
At about 0.2 nats per token from the base, theta1.5 stays below the confusion-trap level, so word-salad tails stay rare.
